findings.finding: The Q1 FY27 10-Q (Note 6) says Deckers paid ~$120M gross of IEEPA tariffs, began filing for refunds under CAPE Phase 2 only after 2026-06-30, and had booked no receivable as of the 10-Q date. Management said guidance includes no refunds. Peers that filed in the same window recognised refunds in cost of sales in the next quarter: Crocs received ~$20M after June 30 and expected to book it in Q3; Dick's booked $59.0M in the quarter to Aug 1; Columbia and Levi saw large margin benefits. Deckers is GAAP-only, so a Q2 recognition of, say, $60-100M net of manufacturer cost-sharing would add roughly $0.35-0.55 to GAAP EPS against a $1.73-1.78 guide and $1.82 consensus, and would mechanically lift the FY EPS guide that excludes it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Deckers has not reported a refund before. Its prints have traded on the FY guide: -15.2% on 2025-10-23 (weak outlook) and +19.5% on 2026-01-29 (raised guide). Across this repo's other names, a refund that landed in all four cases split the reactions by the direction of guidance, not by the refund.
findings.why_not_priced: The $120M gross figure is public, but consensus EPS of $1.82 is only 2% above the top of the company's ex-refund guide, about the size of DECK's usual beat (8/8 beats, average +28%). A refund in the quarter would be visible as a consensus well above $2.00 or as previews modelling it, and none does (the Footwear News preview expects 'in-line' EPS and a reiterated FY range). The market can still look through a one-off, which is why the size is small.
findings.independence: Peer recognition timing comes from different documents: Crocs 10-Q https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001334036/000133403626000052/crox-20260630.htm ; Dick's 10-Q https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001089063/000108906326000036/dks-20260801.htm ; CBP reported ~$122B certified for payment by mid-September (https://www.chrobinson.com/zh-cn/resources/insights-and-advisories/client-advisories/2026q3/09-17-26-cbp-cape-phase-3-ieepa-refunds/). The exclusion from guidance is in the Q1 call transcript (https://www.webull.com/news/15344470755337216).

findings.finding: Deckers bought back $338M of stock in Q1 at an average $103.79, has $4.7B of authorisation left (about 40% of the ~$11.9B market cap), and guides to buybacks of ~80% of FY27 free cash flow. The stock then traded roughly $78-100 through Q2 (it was $78.24 on 2026-09-30), so the same dollars retire more shares. That supports Q2 and FY EPS, and Williams Trading's Sam Poser said the FY EPS guide could be raised partly on buybacks.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY27: a $338M buyback and a 5c EPS guide raise produced a -0.2% close-to-close move (it reportedly fell ~6% after hours first). Buyback-driven EPS raises have not been paid for on their own here.
findings.why_not_priced: The buyback policy is public and the 80%-of-FCF assumption is in the guide. What is not known is the Q2 share count. If the market had priced a guide raise on lower-priced buybacks, consensus FY EPS would sit above $7.50 (it is $7.50, the top of the range).
findings.independence: Remaining authorisation and Q1 average price are confirmed in 10-Q Note 8 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000910521/000091052126000022/deck-20260630.htm), which shares a document with finding 1. Poser's view: https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/could-deckers-second-quarter-earnings-203253701.html

findings.finding: Short interest doubled into the print: 11.81M shares (8.71% of float, 3.2 days to cover) at the 2026-09-30 settlement, against ~5.8M in mid-July, and up 24.9% in the second half of September alone at a $78.24 price. The stock has since risen to $87.36, with the 25d skew at -10.4 (calls bid).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The two most recent upside reactions (+19.46% on 2026-01-29, +11.35% on 2025-07-24) both came off depressed prices with shorts present. The downside reactions (-15 to -20%) came on guide cuts.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the call-bid skew says the option market sees the squeeze. The ~12% October rally on a 2x-larger short base suggests covering has started but is not finished (days to cover is 3.2 on a 2.5M ADV). A short that had already covered would show up as a 10-15 settlement back near July levels, which is not yet published.
findings.independence: Baseline skew -10.44 and run-up +11.03% (sealed baseline file) point the same way, but they are market data, not a separate thesis.

findings.finding: The street is reset low and sits only marginally above the company's Q2 guide. Evercore ISI cut its target to $90 from $108 on 2026-10-16 (In-Line), Raymond James to $105 from $120 the same day, and Telsey reiterated Market Perform at $105 on 10-15. The Footwear News preview (2026-10-20) expects 'few surprises', in-line EPS and a reiterated FY range. Q2 EPS consensus is $1.79-1.82 against a $1.73-1.78 guide, and DECK has beaten EPS consensus 8 of 8 quarters (average +28%) and revenue 6 of 7 (+3.7%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beats are routine and have not protected the stock. The 2025-10-23 Q2 beat fell 15.2% on the outlook, and 2025-05-22 fell 19.9%. The quarter itself is not what DECK trades on.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. This is wire copy, filed because it sets the bar. A low bar shows up as a smaller downside tail, not as an edge.

findings.finding: Closo Research's UGG search-interest index fell year on year through the summer: August 2026 27.0 vs 38.2 (-29.4%), July 13.5 vs 20.2, June 14.6 vs 36.0. Resale days-to-sell fell 42% y/y, and September/October are not yet published. UGG was $759.6M of the $1.43B Q2 FY26 base, and the FY27 guide assumes UGG up mid-single digits.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: UGG holiday commentary in the October print has moved the stock before: the 2025-10-23 -15.2% followed a cautious H2 outlook.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a niche third-party series that no preview cites. Its weight is small: it is a proxy, it covers search rather than sales, and the Q2 UGG line is mostly fall wholesale sell-in already ordered (management said on 07-23 there were 'no cancellations to the order book'). It bears on the H2 guide, not the quarter. Net of the rest: HOKA (~$690M expected in Q2) would have to slow to offset it.
findings.independence: Analyst caution on UGG and warm weather is mentioned in previews (https://www.gurufocus.com/news/9134420/deck-maintained-by-evercore-isi-group-price-target-lowered-to-90 gives no reason). No company or counterparty confirms weakness, and management's 'no cancellations' cuts against it.

findings.finding: On Holding, HOKA's closest premium-running peer, reported on 2026-08-11, after Deckers last spoke: Q2 sales CHF 850M missed CHF 881M consensus, wholesale growth fell to 12.7% c.c. from 25.1% in Q1, and the FY growth guide was cut to 'low-20s%' from 'at least 23%'. The stock fell 20%. That is a read-through to slowing premium-running wholesale, the channel Deckers says re-accelerates for HOKA in H2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: HOKA growth decelerating from 24% (FY25) to 16% (FY26) to 7.7% (Q1 FY27) is the main bear narrative; Q1's HOKA miss traded flat (-0.2%).
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: DECK fell from ~$100 to $78 between August and end-September. It is filed because it is a counterparty print after the company last spoke. If it were unpriced, DECK would not be 28% off its high on 12x forward earnings.

findings.finding: Nike's Q1 FY27 release (2026-10-01, quarter to Aug 31) showed revenue -4% but NIKE Brand wholesale only -1%, with growth in North America; one secondary source puts NA wholesale at +9% c.c. That is a healthy US wholesale channel, but also a sign Nike is regaining shelf space in the athletic-specialty doors HOKA competes in.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None specific. Competitive share loss to a resurgent Nike is part of the HOKA-deceleration narrative.
findings.why_not_priced: Public for three weeks and mixed in sign. It is filed as a counterparty print after Deckers last spoke. A clearly negative transmission would have shown up as DECK falling after 10-01, but DECK rose ~12% from 09-30.

findings.finding: USTR's Section 301 forced-labour determination put a 12.5% additional tariff on Vietnamese goods from 2026-07-24, as Section 122 lapsed. Deckers raised its go-forward tariff assumption to 12.5% from 10% on 2026-07-23, so the realised rate lands inside the guide. Whether footwear is on the exemption list is unconfirmed.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Tariff cost was the cited cause of the 2025-10-23 -15.2% outlook reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced because it matches the company's own assumption. It would only matter if footwear were exempt, which would mean upside to gross margin, and that is unconfirmed.
findings.independence: Q1 call transcript for the 12.5% assumption: https://www.webull.com/news/15344470755337216

findings.finding: An 8-K on 2026-08-31 amended the 2022 credit agreement: the unsecured revolver rises to $500M, maturity is extended to 2031, the commitment fee is cut, and use is working capital and general corporate purposes. No term loan or draw was disclosed.
findings.why_not_priced: Asked what the money buys: liquidity for a net-cash company in its seasonal inventory build, on cheaper terms. It is not distress and not evidently funding an accelerated buyback, so the sign is zero.

lessons_applied: Rule 2 (one-offs): tariff-refund finding trimmed from +1.0 to +0.7. Its path to the guide is mechanical (the FY EPS guide excludes refunds), but this repo's refund names split by guidance direction.

Rule 5 / priced counterparty: On Holding read-through trimmed from -0.5 to -0.3, since DECK already fell from August to September.
